sentences.text: The name Cryptoclidus translates to "hidden clavicles," referring to the animal's tiny collar bones that were buried within its shoulder girdle.
Its specific epithet, eurymerus, means "wide femur," a label applied because researchers initially mistook the forelimb for a hindlimb.
The largest known individuals measured up to 4 meters in length and weighed between 737 and 756 kilograms.
The genus was first described by Seeley in 1892.
The type species was originally described under the name Plesiosaurus eurymerus.
Fossils have been recovered from the Oxford Clay of Cambridgeshire, England.
The species Cryptoclidus vignalensis, now considered undiagnostic, originates from the Jagua Formation of western Cuba.
A 2016 report described a fragmentary skeleton from Russia, though later research defined it as an intermediate cryptoclidid.
The animal lived during the Middle Jurassic to Late Jurassic periods, specifically from the Callovian to the Oxfordian stages.
Fossils have been found in England, France, and Cuba.
It is debated whether a specific Russian fossil fragment belongs to Cryptoclidus or represents an intermediate form between Cryptoclidus and other cryptoclidids.
